After unveiling iPhone Duo today, Apple has rolled out a suite of new resources to help developers prepare their apps for the company's first foldable iPhone. Here's the rundown.

Apple shares iPhone Duo resources with developers

Apple officially unveiled iPhone Duo this morning at its "Surprise and Shine" event. The device, the company's first foldable phone, was announced alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 with active noise cancellation.

Beyond revealing iPhone Duo to the public and sharing device assets on its design resources platform, Apple has also launched a dedicated page offering a range of resources to help developers get ready for the new foldable device.

Content includes two iPhone Duo group labs, held on September 16 and 17 respectively, plus Q&A sessions on photography and cameras, SwiftUI and UIKit, each with two slots at different times, set for September 23.

In addition, Apple will host iPhone Duo workshops in cities around the world, offering hands-on sessions for developers to optimise their apps and "explore adaptability across screen sizes." These workshops will kick off at the end of this month.

The "Get ready for iPhone Duo" page also lists a number of upcoming tools and documentation, including the Xcode 27.1 beta, "Designing for iPhone Duo" and "Preparing your app for iPhone Duo".

The page also lists the following six videos styled like WWDC sessions:

  • Design for iPhone Duo
  • Prepare your app for iPhone Duo
  • Raise the bar with iPhone Duo
  • Strike a pose with adaptive layouts on iPhone Duo
  • Leverage multiple displays and scenes on iPhone Duo
  • Build a great camera experience for iPhone Duo

You can check out Apple's full suite of developer resources for iPhone Duo here.
